read: Eurostat household electricity prices, cited into the registry (P2.3)

dataset.title: Electricity prices for household consumers - bi-annual data (from 2007 onwards)

why_this_slice: Household band 2500-4999 kWh/year is the closest published band to the domestic bills this calculator starts from, I_TAX is the price a household actually pays, and currency EUR makes the figure native rather than converted for the countries cited here. Non-euro EU members are deliberately NOT cited from this dataset: their Eurostat figure is published in EUR, and embedding it against a local-currency row would be a conversion without an exchange rate this project has not verified (V-07 is open).
verification: The values were read twice: once by extracting the full JSON-stat response with explicit stride arithmetic, and once by re-querying the API with every dimension filtered server-side so each country returns exactly one value. The two reads agree, which is what rules out a mis-indexed extraction.

licence.finding: Reuse of statistical data for commercial or non-commercial purposes is authorised provided the source is acknowledged (Commission Decision of 12 December 2011); editorial content is CC BY 4.0. No non-commercial or no-derivatives term appears, so the values are embeddable under R-DATA-04, and each row's note acknowledges the source.

observed_and_not_used: NL reports I_TAX (0.244) below X_TAX (0.2681). That is Eurostat's own figure, not an extraction slip - the filtered re-query returns the same pair - and it is consistent with a tax credit that can leave the tax-inclusive price below the tax-exclusive one. Recorded here because it looks like an error and the next reader should not have to re-derive that conclusion.
Eurostat geo uses EL for Greece; the registry row is GR, so the code is mapped rather than copied.

Bulgaria (BG) was NOT cited: the API still publishes a BG series in EUR, but whether Bulgaria's own currency is BGN or EUR in this period is a separate question this read does not settle. See the lane status for the open question.
